rationale: The buyer is a specific, named professional — an email deliverability engineer or marketing ops lead at a company running PowerMTA or Postfix — with a demonstrated budget (PowerMTA licenses run $10k+/year). The pain is real and business-critical: deferral errors during IP warming directly impact revenue-generating email campaigns. However, the build gate for operational_autonomy (6, just at the floor of 7) is not met and buildability_with_ai is only moderate (5, below the 6 floor) because meaningful deliverability diagnostics require ingesting SMTP logs and correlating them with real-time ISP feedback loops — not trivially done with a Claude prompt and a form. Validate first: sell a manual audit report at $300-500 to 3-5 customers before automating.
solution_plan: The micro-service is an 'Email Deliverability Deferral Audit' — a structured diagnostic report that tells a PowerMTA operator exactly why Yahoo/AOL is returning TSS04/TSS05 codes and what remediation steps to take, prioritized by likely root cause. The factory builds it as: a Typeform intake (client submits their MTA config, sending volume, deferral logs, IP ages) + a Claude prompt that analyzes the inputs against a curated knowledge base of ISP deferral patterns and generates a PDF-format report. Outreach targets email ops communities (Email Geeks Slack, deliverability subreddits, ServerFault/StackExchange email tags) with the factory drafting replies to relevant threads, queued for Youval's approval before posting. Delivery for the first 5 clients is semi-manual: Youval reviews Claude's draft report before sending (given the technical stakes); after validation, the delivery is fully automated. Billing is a one-time Stripe link ($300-500/audit) or a $150/month monitoring subscription once automated. The honest caveat: if the intake data is insufficient for Claude to diagnose the issue, Youval would need to request clarification — make this explicit in the intake form to minimize back-and-forth.
notes: build_gate operational_autonomy: scored 6, floor is 7 — fails by 1 point. build_gate buildability_with_ai: scored 5, floor is 6 — fails. Total 6.1 is below min_total_to_build (6.5) anyway. Validate recommended: manual audits first to learn the pattern, then automate. Strong B2B signal; worth pursuing if Youval can do 3 manual audits to test demand.
